Vs.

full_judgment:
The respondent No. 2, the City Bank Limited Agrabad Branch, Finlay House, Agrabad PS Double Mooring, Chittagong obtained a decree for Taka 4,64,41,787.50 in Mortgage Suit No. 138 of 1991 against the Mobarak Re-rolling Mills and thereafter filed Mortgagee Execution Case No. 6 of 1997 in the aforesaid court. 

 6. Mr MR Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2, submits that 18-11-99 was not the date fixed for auction and on that date the regular judge was on leave and the judge who passed the order dated 18-11-99 was in-charge and on that date an application was filed which was allowed as per order No. 63 dated 18-11-99 and on 22-11-99 the highest bidder offered to purchase the property at Taka 1,12,00,000 and prayed for setting aside the order No. 63 dated 18-11-99 and the decree holder respondent No. 2 also filed another petition for setting aside the order No. 63 and prayed for fixing the date for open auction and the court by the impugned orders in exercise of his inherent power set aside the wrong order which suffers from gross illegality and the court has the power to right what is wrong. He next submits that in a mortgage execution there is no scope for sale by private negotiation in view of Order XXI rule 65 and therefore, the order No. 65 is ex facie, illegal and without jurisdiction and subsequent order has only corrected wrong order and therefore the subsequent order has caused no injury to anybody. He further submits that this writ petition is not maintainable because the petitioner is not a party either in the suit or in the execution proceeding and he has no legal right in the matter because he has not paid any money or suffered any loss. 

 8. Admitted position is that the execution case has been filed for execution of a mortgage decree and Order XXI rule 65 runs as follows: 

 "65. Save as otherwise prescribed, every sale in execution of a decree shall be conducted by an officer of the court or by such other person as the Court may appoint in this behalf, and shall be made by public auction in manner prescribed." 

 9. Since the Artha Rin Adalat Act has not prescribed any mode of execution of the decree passed in the Artha Rin Adalat rule 65, Order XXI CPC is applicable and a sale thereunder must be by a public auction. The rules 82 to 88 of Order XXI dealt with the sale of immovable property. Rule 83(1) of Order XXI runs as follows: 

 "83( 1) Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment-debtor can satisfy the court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property, or some part thereof, or of any other immovable property of the judgment-debtor, the Court may, on his application, postpone the sale of the property comprised in the order for sale on such terms and conditions for such period as it thinks proper, to enable him to raise the amount" 

 10. Thus rule 83 contemplated private sale also but sub-rule 3 makes sub-rule 1 not applicable in case of enforcement of a mortgage decree. Sub-rule 3 of rule 83 runs as follows: 

 "(3) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property." 

 11. Thus it appears from reading-of sub-rule 3 of rule 83 that in case of execution of a decree for enforcement of a mortgage there is no scope for private sale and therefore it must be sold by public auction. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2 has referred to the case of Lyluri Laxi Subramanyam vs Batchu Viswanadham reported in AIR 1988 Andhra Pradesh 27 wherein it was held that in case of execution of mortgage property by sale the provisions of Order XXI rule 83(1) (2) do not apply as rule 83 sub-rule 3 expressly provides for sale of the mortgage property by public auction only.
